subject.title: MEDIA: directive with absolute local paths outside default media roots silently fails (Telegram)

question: Should this issue be scoped to dropped-MEDIA diagnostics while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 owns root expansion, or should this issue also define a new host-local MEDIA root policy?
rationale: A diagnostics-only fix is narrow, but allowing more absolute host paths changes the file-read/upload security boundary and overlaps the open root-policy work.

options.title: Diagnostics Here, Roots In Canonical Policy
options.body: Keep this issue focused on warn-level reasons and safe user notices while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 or the selected tools.fs.roots design owns root expansion.

options.title: Make This The Root-Policy Item
options.body: Use this issue to define the permanent Telegram MEDIA root contract, then close or redirect the overlapping root-policy issue after maintainer approval.

options.title: Document Managed Roots Only
options.body: Decline root expansion for now and finish by documenting the managed-root boundary plus message-tool workaround.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics Here, Roots In Canonical Policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue focused on warn-level reasons and safe user notices while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 or the selected tools.fs.roots design owns root expansion.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history on the outbound media access policy that controls this security boundary.
